title: Canonical localization of an arbitrary bounded-below exact square
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal A',\mathcal B'$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] in a common universe [def-weil-size-convention], with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Write $K^+(\mathcal C)$ for bounded-below cochain complexes modulo chain homotopy, $q:K^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms, and $K(F)$ for termwise application of an additive functor. Let $L:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, $L':\mathcal B'\to\mathcal A'$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$ and $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ be exact additive functors. Put $E=D(L)$, $E'=D(L')$, $T=D(G)$ and $S=D(H)$, with their canonical natural localization isomorphisms $\phi_{F,V}:D(F)(qV)\xrightarrow{\sim}qK(F)V$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Let $\sigma:L'G\to HL$ be an arbitrary natural transformation, and let $\sigma^K:K(L')K(G)\to K(H)K(L)$ be its termwise transformation on $K^+$. For $N\in K^+(\mathcal B)$ put
$$A_N=\phi_{L',K(G)N}\circ E'(\phi_{G,N}),\qquad B_N=\phi_{H,K(L)N}\circ S(\phi_{L,N}).$$ Then there is a unique natural transformation $\theta:E'T\to SE$ between the restrictions of these two composites to $D^+(\mathcal B)$ (functors $D^+(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal A')$) such that for every $N\in K^+(\mathcal B)$,
$$B_N\circ\theta_{qN}=q(\sigma^K_N)\circ A_N.$$
Its component is $\theta_{qN}=B_N^{-1}\circ q(\sigma^K_N)\circ A_N$, so it is the canonical termwise-derived transformation $D(\sigma)$. No invertibility of $\sigma$ or enough-injectives assumption is required.

proof.text: Work directly in the homotopy category. Form the natural transformation τ from K(G)K(L') to K(L)K(H) by composing mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso.hom, NatTrans.mapHomotopyCategory σ, and the inverse composite comparison. Compose and whisker the exact-functor isomorphisms mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh to obtain a: Qh ⋙ (D(G) ⋙ D(L')) ≅ (K(G) ⋙ K(L')) ⋙ Qh and b: Qh ⋙ (D(L) ⋙ D(H)) ≅ (K(L) ⋙ K(H)) ⋙ Qh. Their components are exactly A_N and B_N of the statement.

source.place: mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh; composition with the canonical Functor.associator isomorphisms.

proof.text: Let δ = a.hom followed by whiskerRight τ Qh followed by b.inv, and restrict it along HomotopyCategory.Plus.ι B. The bounded-below homotopy localization Qh⁺ has fully faithful precomposition, so take the preimage θ of this restricted transformation under Localization.fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft. Its source and target are the prescribed unbounded derived composites restricted to D⁺(B), since Qh⁺ ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.ι is definitionally the homotopy inclusion followed by Qh. The bounded-below localization instance already exists in DerivedCategory/Plus.lean and requires no enough-injectives assumption; the cochain quotient and its composite localization are unnecessary here.

source.place: QhCompιIsoιCompQh, lines 108–109; Qh.IsLocalization at HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso, lines 124–126 (the homotopy localization used by the cochain-localization dependency). Preimage: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Predicate.lean, fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft.

proof.text: Evaluate the fully faithful structure's map_preimage equation at N. It gives θ_(qN) = a_N ≫ Qh(τ_N) ≫ b_N⁻¹. Expanding only the composite isomorphisms and simplifying identity maps gives exactly the displayed second equality. Postcompose with b_N and use b_N⁻¹ ≫ b_N = 1 to get the first equality. This cancels only the canonical comparison isomorphism, with no inverse of σ.

source.place: Functor.FullyFaithful.map_preimage; evaluate with congr_app and cancel using Iso.inv_hom_id_app.

proof.text: For any other θ' satisfying the two equalities, its second equality and the component formula for θ give equality at every Qh⁺(N). Apply Localization.natTrans_ext to the bounded-below homotopy localization to conclude θ' = θ. Thus the constructed transformation is unique.
